intro.text: A gang of robbers whose crimes are written up in Elendel's broadsheets.
A criminal gang led by Miles Dagouter that robs trains and high-society gatherings, stealing cargo and valuables and carrying off women as hostages.
A criminal gang used by the Set to rob shipments that House Tekiel had insured and to abduct women of Allomantic descent for its Community.

description.text: When they raid a society gathering they search everyone thoroughly, even making people talk to check for jewels hidden in their mouths, and try to avoid violence. They carry off one or more women, making the choice look random, and threaten to kill them if anyone follows.
The broadsheets cover them at length, quoting witnesses and experts without learning much. Miles sees the publicity as vital, since it makes the constables look helpless.
Miles Dagouter leads them, and Clamps and Tarson are his most trusted men.
Except for Miles they go unmasked, in loose shirts, slacks and vests. They carry rifles and pistols, some made of aluminum and loaded with aluminum bullets.

They halt a train by blocking the line where it runs near the canal, first with a fallen tree, then with a phantom engine: a hand-driven rail wagon behind a wooden front and a bright lamp, helped by the mists. A crane on a canal barge then swaps the target car for an empty copy, so the cargo vanishes with no forced locks or dead guards.

items.text: Their first train robbery, on 14 Vinuarch 341 PC, took a shipment of House Tekiel's aluminum. After four months in hiding they robbed six more trains, two of them House Ladrian's, taking steel, food and many other metals. They soon began robbing passenger cars too, for valuables and captives.
When the wealthy women of Allomantic descent that the Set had picked out stopped riding trains, the gang robbed the Coolerim Playhouse to seize its next target, Armal Harms.
The gang burst into the Yomen-Ostlin wedding dinner, stripped every guest of their valuables and loudly took Steris and Marasi as captives. Their leader shot Lord Peterus for objecting.

In the fight that followed, Wax and Wayne freed Marasi, killed twenty-five bandits and left six to be arrested. Wax shot both Tarson and the leader, but neither was badly hurt, and the survivors escaped with Steris. Lord Peterus was the only guest killed.
The constables learned nothing from the six captured bandits, but Wayne, posing as a constable, got useful information out of them.
The gang abandoned its old base, a foundry in Longard, and moved its forging equipment to a new hideout underground. The explosive traps they left behind were easily disarmed by Wax and Wayne.

Miles met Suit, who funded the operation and was displeased that killing Peterus had drawn Wax in. Suit planned a raid on House Tekiel's new Breaknaught railcar, and Miles promised to kill Wax, but his attack on Wax's train failed.

Suit told Miles that the Breaknaught robbery would be their last before six months in hiding to recruit, and that Wax must die during it. Steris was kept at the hideout as bait, and Suit left Miles two Allomancers of his own, Push and Pull. Half the stolen aluminum was to go to Suit's people.

Using their phantom engine, the Vanishers stopped the train, gunned down the Tekiel guards with a rotary gun and swapped the Breaknaught for the Set's copy. They took it back to their base near the Ironspine Building, not knowing Wax had rigged its door with explosives. The blast let him slip out and start taking them down.

Wayne and Marasi soon joined him. Together they took down every Vanisher except Miles, freed the gunsmith Nouxil and sent Steris for the constables, while Marasi held Miles in a time bubble until the constables arrived to seize him.
For his help on the case, the constables granted Wax a citywide deputised forbearance, backdated to cover what he had done, and let Wayne off for impersonating an officer.
Miles was executed by firing squad. Wax discovered that Suit was his uncle Edwarn, who had used the robberies to defraud House Tekiel, buying up its debts while sure the goods would be given back.
The women the Vanishers had taken stayed with the Set and became part of its Community.
